clue.text: European in Wagner production, including Ring

indicators.note: including means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside them
a production of the composer's name and the little word before it means those letters are staged afresh in a new order

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A continental visitor sits in a staging of Wagner that includes his Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' gives NRWEGIAN and 'including' sets the ring's O after its first letter. Wagner's Ring cycle is the false trail: the Ring is only a round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Norway is a person from a European country.

clue.text: Plutocrat raised an insignificant amount of money once

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the little word an is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, a small pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A rich man raised a tiny sum long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling, a pre-1971 British coin worth a twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very wealthy man, originally one who made a fortune in India.

clue.text: Representative members of RAF? Cobblers!

parts.note: airmen are members of the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses airmen as RAF representatives with a cry of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers!' is British slang for nonsense, but here it means shoe-menders.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers mend shoes, so they are tradesmen who fix things.

clue.text: At the maximum point of shock, one interrupts silly pretence

indicators.note: interrupts means the numeral for one breaks into the rearranged letters
silly means the letters of pretence are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: At the height of an earthquake, someone breaks off a foolish pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges PRETENCE into EPCENTRE and 'interrupts' puts I after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the ground above an earthquake's origin, where the tremor is strongest.

clue.text: It takes less than a year to generate such interest

definitions.text: It takes less than a year to generate such interest

parts.words: It takes less than a year to generate such interest
parts.note: interest here is a company's payout to shareholders, the half-year one paid before the year's accounts close

explanation.surface: A banker explains a short-term return on savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' reads as savings interest; it is a dividend paid partway through a company's financial year.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment to shareholders made partway through the year, before annual results, a part-year return.

clue.text: Country's views canvassed here?

parts.note: reads as an opinion poll of the nation; really the views are paintings on canvas owned by the nation

explanation.surface: A question about where public opinion is surveyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' are landscapes and 'canvassed' means painted on canvas; the London museum holds the nation's pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The London art museum on Trafalgar Square holds the nation's collection of paintings.

clue.text: Fill to the brim to produce litter

parts.note: taken as written
to pup is to give birth to a litter of young, as a dog does

explanation.surface: An instruction that seems to mix filling a glass with an animal giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish something until it is completely full is the phrasal verb used of glasses and tanks.

clue.text: Animal half-hearted in comparison with fictional counterpart

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two middle letters, half of the heart, is lost

parts.note: Tigger is the bouncing striped friend of Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A real beast seems feeble beside its storybook version.
explanation.walkthrough: TIGGER has a double G at its heart; 'half-hearted' removes one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The big striped cat is an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Aid to climbing in ostentatiously good fashion

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, showily virtuous
ton means fashion or style, as in the phrase bon ton

explanation.surface: A climbing aid described as smugly good and stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal spike driven into rock to hold a rope is a mountaineer's support.

clue.text: Make a joke lightly, but with sarcasm

parts.note: to pun is to make a joke playing on words
gently means lightly or softly

explanation.surface: Advice to joke gently, though with a sarcastic edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharply caustic speech is biting, a sense shared with sarcastic remarks.

clue.text: Who christened John?

parts.note: reads as asking who baptised someone called John; really it asks what name John the evangelist's namesake, the Jordan preacher, was given as his title

explanation.surface: A Bible-quiz question about who baptised John.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks who performed a christening; the answer is the epithet attached to John the forerunner of Jesus, and also a member of a church that practises adult immersion.
explanation.definitionFit: John the forerunner of Jesus is known by the title meaning one who immerses converts in water.

clue.text: When speaking, great man is tense

indicators.note: when speaking signals that the word for the great man is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a titan is a person of huge stature or importance

explanation.surface: A remark that an important man is nervous and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective describing the great man, but it is the verb, meaning to stiffen.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen or make taut a muscle is a verb meaning to draw it firmer.

clue.text: Live with wife in square

indicators.note: in means the word for a wife goes inside the word for living

parts.note: to live or exist is to be
rib for a wife is a crossword convention from the story of Eve made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: Advice to settle down and live with your wife in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' wants to be a noun, a public space; here it is the verb meaning to buy someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To square an official is slang for paying a corrupt inducement to win their cooperation.

clue.text: Drive, carrying old relative to part of Mexican border

indicators.note: carrying means the word for a drive holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a drive in a car is a ride
a gran is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: Someone drives an elderly relative down to the Mexican frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river forms much of the frontier between Texas and Mexico.

clue.text: Let in millions through mine entrance

indicators.note: through means the letter for millions passes inside the word for the mine entrance

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions of people are allowed in through the entrance of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: ADIT, a near-horizontal mine entrance, is a word mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow someone entry is the same as permitting them to come inside.

clue.text: Sworn statement from staff I'd a vital part in it

indicators.note: part in it means the answer is a part held within the words just before

explanation.surface: A sworn statement in which staff say they played a vital role.
explanation.definitionFit: A written declaration confirmed on oath for use as evidence in court.

clue.text: Most unfair way introduced as method to establish need

indicators.note: introduced means the abbreviation for a way is put inside the word for most unfair

parts.note: meanest means most ungenerous or unfair
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the harshest method was brought in to judge who needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: A means test is the British check on income and savings before state benefit is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The assessment of a person's income decides whether they qualify for benefit, gauging their need.

clue.text: Dreadful parvenu, and so explosive, this star

indicators.note: dreadful means the letters of the two words are made into an awful jumble

explanation.surface: A dreadful upstart, a volatile celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had a stray apostrophe after 'this'. 'Dreadful' is the anagram signal; 'star' looks like a celebrity but is the heavenly body.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding star that suddenly flares to enormous brightness.

clue.text: Mill, for instance, comes into production

indicators.note: production means the letters of the two words are worked into a new product

explanation.surface: A factory mill starts producing goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mill' looks like a factory; it is John Stuart Mill, the Victorian political economist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a political economist, an expert on the science of wealth.

clue.text: Handling fine wool

definitions.meaning: touching or feeling something with the hands
a fine knitting yarn of the same name

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling with the fingers is touching; it is also the name of a thin knitting yarn.

clue.text: Run into rotten agent

indicators.note: into means the letter for run goes inside the word for rotten

parts.note: poxy is British slang for rotten or worthless
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A bitter complaint about meeting a useless representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into' reads as a phrasal verb meaning meet, but 'Run' gives R and 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone authorised to vote or act for another is their deputy or representative.

clue.text: Line dance moves recurring regularly

indicators.note: moves in a dance suggests the letters of the two words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Line-dancing steps that come round again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' looks like a noun, the steps of the dance, but it is the anagram signal on LINE DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something occurring every ten years recurs at fixed intervals, hence regularly.

clue.text: Butterfly found in every list?

definitions.meaning: an orange butterfly with ragged wings and a white mark under them
the punctuation that separates items in a list

explanation.definitionFit: It names a ragged-winged butterfly and the punctuation mark separating listed items.

clue.text: Snare set up without delay at front of earth

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word for without delay is read upwards

parts.note: soon means without delay, shortly

indicators.note: front of means only the opening letter of earth is used

explanation.surface: A trapper quickly sets a snare at the edge of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SOON into NOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope that tightens when pulled is used as a trap.

clue.text: Perch in river circles beside stone

parts.note: two circles look like two letter Os
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: A fish swims in a river round and round beside a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' suggests the fish in the river, but it is the bird's resting place. Stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to rest, the same as their resting bar.

clue.text: Actual wording used by singer

definitions.meaning: the exact words of a legal document
a high male voice in a choir

explanation.definitionFit: It means the exact wording of a document in law, and a high male voice.

clue.text: Split low in container

indicators.note: in means the cow's sound sits inside the word for a container

parts.note: a vase is a container for flowers
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A vessel cracks apart at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as cracked, and 'low' as an adjective; 'Split' is slang for leave and 'low' is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To split is slang for leaving quickly, the same as clearing off.

clue.text: There's one book going around concerned with passion

indicators.note: going around means the word for a book is turned to read the other way

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about or concerned with, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A single book doing the rounds is all about passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' gives EMOT; 'There's' only joins the wordplay to the definition, and 'passion' is a strong feeling rather than an enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as love or anger is a passion, a feeling of the heart.

clue.text: Discover whereabouts of some harness

definitions.meaning: to track down or locate someone
one of the two straps by which a horse pulls a cart

explanation.definitionFit: To locate someone is to track them down; it is also a strap linking a draught horse to its load.

clue.text: Corrupt, sly trader who dealt in chemicals?

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of the next two words are spoiled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A dishonest, cunning merchant who traded in chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective on the trader, but it rearranges SLY TRADER. A drysalter sold dyes, salts and preserving chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: An old trade name for a dealer in dyes, gums and salting chemicals.
